You can only apply for one term (either autumn or spring) to QUT

Studies and making your study plan

  1. Approved study units = All students can study these units, regardless of your academic background.
  2. Units requiring approval = You can only enrol in these units if you meet the specified requirements and have significant background knowledge in the area of study. After you apply, we will assess the units and your background knowledge and let you know the outcome.

Please note that undergraduate level students cannot take graduate level courses. Letters N and P in the course code mean that the course will be on postgraduate level.

The faculties at QUT will make the final decision on which courses can be offered to the applicants.

The student must choose at least 6 courses (units) in the study plan. 4 courses per semester, is however, considered full study load. Courses are usually worth 12 credits and this means 7,5 ECTS. Please note that the final decision on credit transfer will always be made in the student's own degree programme in Aalto University.

Eligibility criteria

The student must have a GPA of at least 3,13 / 5,00.
The student must have completed at least 1 year of full-time study at Aalto.

Language requirements

You do not need a language test result if

  • You have completed a bachelor's or master's a degree at Aalto in a programme in which the language of instruction is English.
  • 1 year of full-time studies with a passing GPA at Aalto and a pass in English subject from Finnish High School (Note that both elements of this requirement must have been completed within five years of the intended start date at QUT) Use your paper highschool diploma, not the one from Opintopolku because we cannot guarantee that QUT accepts the latter.

Else you will need one of the following:

  • IELTS (Academic): An overall score of 6.5, and no sub-score less than 6.0
  • TOEFL (Internet-based): An overall score of 79 (writing 21, reading 16, listening 16, speaking 18)
  • Pearson Test of English (PTE Academic): An overall score of 58, and no sub-score less than 50
  • Cambridge English: Advanced (CAE): An overall score of 176, and no sub-score less than 169
  • Cambridge English: Proficiency (CPE): Grade of C1

Other

Please note that the semesters run differently in Australia. Spring semester is semester 1 and autumn semester is semester 2 in Australia. Summer holiday run from December to January. However, Aalto students apply according to the Finnish semesters.

The student applies for the visa after an official acceptance from QUT. Accepted exchange students must also pay for the Overseas Student Health Cover fee (approx. AUD 350).

You can only apply for one term (either autumn or spring) to RMIT.

Eligibility criteria

Please see the webpage for complete and always up-to-date instructions: Student exchange

At the time of application you must

  • have completed at least one full year of studies at your home institution (i.e. min. 60 ECTS)
  • have a GPA of at least 3,00 / 5,00
  • have minimum of B2-level in English

English language requirement: See how to prove B2 level in Aalto's application round here.


Studies and making your study plan

How to search for courses (Course search link can be found here).

Please note that choosing the recommended courses is advisable for an exchange student.

Students can choose courses quite freely as long as they meet the RMIT prerequisites for the courses and the degree programme at Aalto approves the study plan. The student should select 8 courses for his/her study plan. 4 courses per semester, is however, considered full study load (and usually the maximum number of courses the student can actually take). Courses are usually worth 12 credits, i.e. 7,5 ECTS.

Undergraduate students can take some postgraduate courses if they have studied full-time for three years. RMIT will check if the student fulfills the prerequisites etc. during their own application procedure. When you prepare your study plan, please check that the chosen courses are offered for the same class, same semester and same campus. RMIT has three different campus areas in Melbourne and because of the distance you have to choose your courses from one campus. And if you choose courses from different levels/class timetable clashes may occur. Course choices have to be made very carefully already for the Aalto application!

Please note the restrictions, e.g. arts & design courses are only for students in these fields. Note that most of the Postgraduate courses require completion of a Bachelor degree.

NOT OPEN FOR APPLICATIONS FOR THE ACADEMIC YEAR 2024/25. No places left in the September 2023 supplementary application round either.

You can only apply for one term (either autumn or spring) to USYD.

Making your study plan:

Please choose at least four units of study (24 credit points) per semester for your study plan. Undergraduate units of study have the numbers 1000-3000 appearing in the course code. Codes in the 1000 range typically correspond to first year study, 2000s to second year study and 3000s to third year study. Codes for postgraduate students are typically numbered 5000-6000 level.

Undergraduate students are only permitted to select undergraduate units (those with unit codes 1000, 2000 or 3000 level). There are a handful of postgraduate engineering units which some undergraduate students may be eligible to select if they’re in their final year and subject to faculty approval. But generally speaking, postgraduate units are closed to undergraduate students. Postgraduate students however, are eligible to select both undergraduate and postgraduate units.

You can select units across multiple faculties.

Eligibility criteria: GPA of at least 3,75 / 5,00

Language requirements:

KU Leuven stands out as one of Europe’s most distinguished universities, renowned for its 600-year tradition of academic excellence and its position as Belgium’s largest and highest-ranked university. Unlike many European institutions, KU Leuven offers over 100 English-taught programmes across 15 faculties, all consistently ranked in the global top 100 for their fields. This breadth of high-quality, internationally oriented education attracts a diverse student body, with nearly 24% of its 63,000 students coming from over 150 countries, fostering a truly global academic environment.

Leuven, the university’s home city, is a vibrant student hub where the campus and city life are seamlessly integrated. With a population of around 100,000—nearly a third of whom are students—Leuven offers a lively, youthful atmosphere, characterised by historic architecture, pedestrian-friendly streets, and a thriving cultural scene. The city is compact, safe, and easily navigable by bike or on foot, with affordable living costs compared to other European student cities. Leuven’s central location in Belgium also provides unparalleled access to Brussels (just 20 minutes by train) and major European capitals like Paris, Amsterdam, and Cologne, making it an ideal base for travel and international networking

Belgium itself is a multicultural, multilingual crossroads at the heart of Europe, offering students a unique blend of Dutch, French, and German influences alongside widespread English proficiency. As the seat of the European Union and NATO, Belgium provides unmatched opportunities for internships, networking, and post-graduation careers in international organisations.

The Katholieke Universiteit Leuven (KU Leuven) is a research university in the Dutch-speaking town of Leuven in Flanders, 25 kilometres from Brussels (about 20-30 minutes by train). Leuven could be described as a large-sized Otaniemi with a lively student culture, and a safe living environment.

Studies and making your study plan

Under each subject area courses are divided into Undergraduate and Advanced/master's level courses. To be eligible for courses at Advanced/Master's level, you usually need a bachelor degree of 3 years and/or three years of studies within the subject area. There will also be specific requirements in the course information. Advanced/master’s level is marked “A1X” or ”A2X”. The undergraduate level is marked ”G1X” or ”G2X.

Courses are given at two campuses in Linköping and one campus in Norrköping. A free bus connects the campuses. LKPG indicates that the course is given in Linköping, while NKPG indicates Norrköping. A few courses marked LKPG, in particular courses in Biomedical Engineering, are given at the University Hospital Campus in Linköping. Each semester at the Faculty of Science and Engineering is divided into two separate study periods. Ht is an abbreviation of the Swedish word “Hösttermin”, meaning autumn semester. For the autumn semester, the study periods are called Ht1 and Ht2, and for the spring Vt1 and Vt2. Vt is an abbreviation of the Swedish word “Vårtermin” which means spring semester. Courses can be given during one of the individual study periods (Vt1 or Vt2/Ht1 or Ht2) or run for the entire semester (Vt1 and Vt2/Ht1 and Ht2). Within one study period (Vt1 or Vt2/Ht1 or Ht2) you should only choose courses given at the same campus. As an example, it is not possible to follow course X in Linköping and course Y in Norrköping during Vt1. You may however follow all Vt1 courses in Linköping and all Vt2 courses in Norrköping, or vice versa.

Incoming exchange students are required to register for 30 credits per semester, with at least 15 credits at the Faculty of Engineering - LTH. It is allowed to combine courses from different engineering programmes.

 

In the application you'll have to state two alternatives per course (the ones you have primarily chosen). LTH does not have an add & drop period, and course choices cannot be changed unless there is a problem with timetable clashes or other justifiable reason.

Bilateral: École Polytechnique Fédérale (EPF) Lausanne - SCI

Under this agreement, the exchange places available are as follows:

  • two places for computer science
  • one place for mathematics
  • one place for physics
  • Note!! You can not use the same study plan to apply under both EPFL agreements!

Please understand, that exchange at EPF Lausanne requires (very) hard work. 60-70 hours per week is not an exception. This is not a destination for lots of time for leisure or taking it easy. You need to be prepared and you are expected to spend many hours studying. It is also very important to understand that the Aalto students' study success at EPF Lausanne can affect future of the agreement. If there are constantly students who underperform during the exchange (small amount of credits or bad grades), the agreement can be terminated by EPFL, more restrictions can appear or number of places can be diminishded. Please consider your application to EPFL carefully and commit to hard working and completing the selected courses, if applying.

Additional eligibility criteria

  • For practical reasons EPFL wishes Aalto to select the number of applicants in balance for autumn and spring term. This means, that the academic term that you are applying for may affect if you get selected or not in Aalto's internal applicant selections.
  • when applying SCI agreement places to EPFL, it is not allowed to choose even a single course from Management of Technology and Financial Engineering.
  • Please note the visa requiements mentioned in the guidelines

Bilateral: Eidgenössische Technische Hochschule (ETH) Zürich - SCI (LIFE)

ETH Zurich is ranked as one of the best universities in the world and the leading university in continental Europe. In the 2021 edition of QS World University Rankings, ETH Zurich was ranked 6th in the world, placing it as the second-best European university after the University of Oxford. As of November 2021, 21 Nobel laureates, 2 Fields Medalists, 2 Pritzker Prize winners, and 1 Turing Award winner have been affiliated with the Institute, including Albert Einstein.

ETH Zurich has two campuses. The main building is located right in the heart of the city: the Zentrum campus consists of various buildings and institutions throughout Zürich and firmly integrates the ETH Zurich in the city. A new campus was built on the Hönggerberg on a northern hill in the outskirts of the city. The ETH link is a free bus for students, affiliates and faculty linking the two campuses. Studying at ETHZ is can be hard work - the undergraduates' tight curriculum consists of as much as twice the number of lectures as comparable courses of other Swiss universities.

Additional eligibility criteria

  • these ETHZ places are only for students in Life Science Technologies Master Programme
  • students must have completed at least 2 years/120 ECTS of their studies at university level in a relevant study field before the planned start of the exchange period.
  • for better chances to get accepted, applicants should have earned a solid amount of credits with better than avarage GPA by the time of applying to ETHZ. ETH Zurich reserves the right to decline applications from students who have only recently started their studies at the sending institution and have not yet been able to establish a solid academic track record there, which is necessary in order to assess their ability to successfully study at ETH Zurich.
  • Applicants need to prepared and committed to work hard during the exchange. A workload of 30 ECTS and over may be overwhelming, not being used to ETH’s highly demanding academic environment.

The National Taiwan University of Science and Technology was founded on August 1, 1974. It was the first higher education institution of its kind within our nation’s technical and vocational education system. By extending this system to the highest level, this new school was intended to meet the need created by our rapid economic and industrial development for highly trained bachelor’s degree-level engineers and managers. In 1979 and 1982, NTIT added master’s and doctoral programs, respectively.

The University offers English-taught classes for graduate-level students and free Mandarin learning program for foreign students.

National Taiwan University of Science and Technology (Taiwan Tech) is the first technological University in Taiwan. Taiwan Tech is located in Taipei downtown area which is about 10-minute walk from Gong-Guan MRT (mass rapid transit) station. The one-year program, from August till August, consists of one semester for exchange studies, and another semester for Master's thesis + three one-week coaching modules.

Students enrolled in a Master's programme (excl. international joint programmes) at CHEM, ELEC, ENG or SCI may apply. First year studies in one's own Master's programme must be completed when starting in the UNITECH program.

Bilateral: Pace University, Seidenberg School of Computer Science and Information Systems - ELEC, SCI

No places available for application to Pace University for 2026-27.

Students from the School of Electrical Engineering and School of Science can apply for exchange to New York. Students from the other Technical Schools of Aalto can be admitted if the spots are not used by ELEC and SCI.

Studies and making your study plan

Pace University has two campus areas: New York City and a more traditional college campus Pleasantville - Please choose your courses from one campus! Please note that you will have to choose at least 2/3 of your courses from Seidenberg School of Computer and Information Systems. Also, pay attention to the possible prerequisites. Usual workload: UG min. 12 credits, G min. 9 credits. However, please remember Aalto's requirement for the study plan (30 ECTS per semester)! Courses in the School of Performing Arts in the Film and Screen Studies and Law are not open for exchange students. Lubin School of Business is not open to graduate level exchange students.

Students must provide 5 preferred course selections and 5 alternate course options.

Local credits 1 Pace credit = 2 ECTS. However, the official credit transfer will be made after the exchange.

Please note that as an undergraduate student you are required to have completed at least two years of study at Aalto before the exchange.
